newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SGB Davignon welcomes GBL's Frere in Suez.
newsitem.headline: SGB Davignon welcomes GBL's Frere in Suez.

text.p: Etienne Davignon, chairman of the board of Belgian Ste Generale de Belgique (SGB), welcomed the entry of rival holding company Groupe Bruxelles Lambert (GBL) in the capital of SGB's French parent Compagnie de Suez.
"It is a good thing for Suez, and Mr. Frere's entry in Suez will not alter the relationship between Suez and SGB," Davignon told Reuters in an interview on Thursday.
Belgian businessman Albert Frere's GBL late last year acquired a minority stake in Suez, leading to speculation that Frere may have designs on SGB.
Frere already has a 2.03 percent direct stake in SGB via GBL unit Compagnie Nationale a Portefeuille (CNP) NAPO.BR.
"Mr Frere knows SGB well via CNP, he must think that Suez is a good investment," Davignon said.
Between them SGB and GBL together control virtually all the key sectors of the Belgian economy, such as banking, utilities, energy, insurance and several industrial blue chip companies.
When Frere, as expected, takes a seat on Suez' board this year or next, the relationship between Belgium's two best-known businessmen will change radically.
Frere is a self-made millionaire of humble origin, while Viscount Davignon is an aristocrat with family links to Belgium's oldest and wealthiest families.
Once Frere becomes a board member of Suez -- which holds 62 percent of SGB -- he will have a say in how SGB is run.
That new authority will be the culmination of a lifelong battle to the top, a battle which most of the time has pitted him against SGB.
GBL unit Electrafina bought a 2.9 percent stake in Suez in October and raised it to 5.06 percent in December.
Suez chief executive officer Gerard Mestrallet has invited Frere to boost his stake further and has said he would welcome Frere on the Suez board.
